accuracy.reason: All nine card objectives are accurately scoped: embedded persistence/locality, affinity and STRICT constraints, configured ACID, single writer/busy handling, WAL/checkpoints, query costs, supported backups/migrations and workload choice. Live SQLite primary documents confirm the distinctions without numerical capacity promises.

evidence.quote: WAL still allows only one writer, and its shared-memory design requires processes on the same machine.

mechanisms.reason: Cards 1-2 locate SQL execution and files; 3-4 connect enforced rules and transaction boundaries to flush/locking assumptions; 5-6 explain competing writers, busy retries, snapshots and checkpoint growth; 7 connects indexes to access/order; 8 traces WAL backup hazards and operational obligations; 9 integrates them into a deployment decision.

evidence.quote: Committed data may still be in the WAL, so copying only the main file can omit required state.

coherence.reason: All nine objective/prerequisite edges are met in order. Embedded/server comparison, single-writer queue, WAL-to-checkpoint and owner/date index diagrams match zero-based slides 0,4,5,6. They illustrate rather than imply distributed multi-writer access or automatic backup completeness.

evidence.quote: SQLite changes where the database runs. You still have a relational database.

decisions.reason: Provides qualified local/server placement, explicit FK verification, bounded contention response, WAL limits, measured indexes, supported consistent backups and restoration testing. No user-count shortcut or unprovided retry/backup implementation is required to meet the conceptual criteria.

evidence.quote: One writer per database, responsibility for local files, and additional work if data must synchronize across machines.

clarity.reason: Embedded/serverless, affinity, storage class, STRICT, ACID, busy, WAL and checkpoint are defined before use. Source links and diagrams are meaningful; shared renderer and relevant CSS were inspected once, not run. Examples clarify independent mechanisms without forced story continuity.

evidence.quote: Transfers logged changes into the main database file. Long-running reads can delay checkpoint progress and allow the log to grow.

outcomes.reason: All six criteria supported across actual answers: library-call/process boundary, persistent relational file and in-memory option, application/host operational ownership (explicit in query-plan answer), local/offline fit, shared-network concurrency reason for server evaluation, workload rather than user/size threshold and no automatic device sync.

All eight criteria supported: ordinary affinity/storage classes versus STRICT/ANY; PK/UNIQUE/NOT NULL/CHECK; per-connection pre-transaction FK enable/verify; required-value and business-logic limits; commit/rollback atomicity and declared consistency; isolation with races/waits; configured flush/storage durability; external actions excluded.

All eight criteria supported: many connections/one writer, competing access and BUSY, short transactions without slow network work, bounded waits/transaction retries without success guarantee, original-data rollback versus separate WAL, stable readers with one writer, checkpoint/long-reader growth, same-host shared-memory/locking limits. Missing detailed busy codes is outside scope.

All eight criteria supported: index and plan, owner-then-time candidate plus EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN/measurement, scan discretion and local CPU/I/O/memory/write costs, permissions/space, coordinated migrations, consistent supported backup accounting for WAL, retained backups and actual restore/usability/time testing. A quiescent-copy procedure is optional because supported consistent backup is an accepted alternative.

All four criteria supported: conditional short-write single-host fit, multi-server sustained-writer reason to evaluate server DB, WAL supplies neither multiple writers nor sync, explicit integrity/transaction/query/recovery duties and measured contention/duration/deployment/query/recovery requirements. No invented numeric threshold is demanded.

sourceChecks.claim: Inspected SQLite appropriate-use description: engine built into application, local storage and application-server hosting; no mandatory separate SQL service. File ownership and recovery follow from deployment model.
Inspected appropriate-use local devices, command-line/server cases and multi-computer/competing-write guidance. Workload/locality rather than universal user cutoff is supported.

Inspected STRICT supported conversion/ANY rules; datatype affinity followup defines recommended types/storage classes; foreignkeys followup confirms null allowance, enable/verify and no effect when toggled inside transaction. Required CHECK plus NOT NULL avoids missing-value loophole.

Inspected synchronous pragma durability table and WAL NORMAL/FULL flush behavior. Recent commits can be lost under weaker settings; filesystem and storage behavior matter. Database atomicity does not reverse external side effects.

Inspected isolation single-writer/multiple-connections rule and ordinary visibility. Busy contention and transaction retries follow the access boundary; no guaranteed success or added writer capacity is asserted.

Inspected WAL reader snapshots, writer serialization, checkpoint reader restrictions/growth and same-host shared-memory requirement. Journal versus WAL and transfer to main file are accurately distinguished.

Inspected SQLite queryplanner multi-column ordering and combined filter/sort access examples. Candidate owner/time index and measuring plan work are supported; indexes add storage and write maintenance rather than free local speed.

Inspected SQLite Backup API completed consistent snapshot and WAL persistent-state/copy warning; ALTER TABLE followup rebuild procedure supports coordinated migrations. Retention and restore testing are appropriate application responsibilities.

Inspected appropriate-use network access and simultaneous-writer guidance. A local application server can still fit SQLite; competing writes across machines can favor client/server, with file and recovery obligations retained.
